record.what_it_does: ClickUp is a project management and productivity platform whose Public API lets developers read and manage Workspaces, Spaces, Folders, Lists, tasks, docs, comments, time tracking, and goals.
record.auth_notes: Personal API tokens (prefix `pk_`) are for individual/testing use and are passed directly in the Authorization header (not a standard Bearer scheme prefix); OAuth2 authorization-code flow is used for apps that serve other users, issuing a token used as `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}`. OAuth access tokens currently do not expire, per ClickUp's docs, though this is noted as subject to change.
record.access_notes: Any user can log in to ClickUp (free plan available) and immediately generate a personal API token from Settings > Apps with no approval step. Building an OAuth app for other users requires only Workspace owner/admin status to register the app (client_id/secret), also self-serve with no vendor review mentioned.
record.main_blocker: ClickUp's own MCP server only supports OAuth login (not direct API-key auth) and imposes low daily call caps (50/day on Free plan, 300/day on Unlimited+) unless the Workspace buys the 'Everything AI' add-on; a custom-built toolkit against the REST API instead avoids the MCP-specific caps but should be noted as a design choice.

evidence.quote: For personal use, authenticate with your personal API token... use the OAuth flow, allowing users to authorize Workspaces for your app.
Personal tokens begin with `pk_`. Add the token to the header: `Authorization: {personal_token}`.
Log in to ClickUp... Under API Token, click Generate or Regenerate.
Can I authenticate with my own API keys or Auth access tokens? A. No... We only support OAuth for authentication.
For AI agents: visit https://developer.clickup.com/llms.txt for an index of all pages formatted in Markdown and endpoints in OpenAPI.
The raw OpenAPI specification for the ClickUp API is available for each version of our Public API.
Webhooks allow you to subscribe to events in your Workspace.

record.open_questions: Exact endpoint count for api_breadth wasn't enumerated from the OpenAPI spec itself (only inferred from the broad resource list in webhooks/docs pages: tasks, lists, folders, spaces, goals, docs, comments, time tracking); the V3 API scope beyond V2 wasn't independently verified.
